episodes.156685: A warm front began to lift north across East Texas and North Louisiana during the afternoon of April 13th, with warm, moist, and unstable air shifting back north across these areas. Meanwhile, a weak upper level disturbance in the zonal flow aloft helped enhance scattered thunderstorm development along and north of the front across portions of East Texas. Given the adequate shear and extent of instability aloft, isolated severe thunderstorms developed and produced reports of large hail across these areas before diminishing during the evening with the loss of heating. However, another more significant shortwave trough traversed the Red River Valley of Southern Oklahoma and North Texas, as the warm front shifted farther north across East Texas to near the Louisiana/Arkansas border. Large scale forcing ahead of this trough and elevated instability aloft resulted in an increase in shower and thunderstorm development during the early morning hours of April 14th, near and ahead of an associated cold front that had begun to enter the region from the northwest. A few isolated severe thunderstorms developed over portions of Northeast Texas, Southwest Arkansas, and North Louisiana, producing instances of large hail before these storms weakened and became more numerous after daybreak, before eventually diminishing from west to east by afternoon.
episodes.156688: A warm front began to lift north across East Texas and North Louisiana during the afternoon of April 13th, with warm, moist, and unstable air shifting back north across these areas. During the early morning hours of the 14th, a significant shortwave trough traversed the Red River Valley of Southern Oklahoma and North Texas, as the warm front shifted farther north across East Texas to near the Louisiana/Arkansas border. Large scale forcing ahead of this trough and elevated instability aloft resulted in an increase in shower and thunderstorm development, near and ahead of an associated cold front that had begun to enter the region from the northwest. A few isolated severe thunderstorms developed over portions of Northeast Texas, Southwest Arkansas, and North Louisiana, producing instances of large hail. In North Louisiana, an isolated severe thunderstorm produced quarter size hail in Dry Prong. These storms weakened and became more numerous after daybreak, before eventually diminishing from west to east by afternoon.

episodes.157410: A thunderstorm produced non-severe hail in Dallas county at Sparkman.
episodes.157589: Heavy rain brought flooding to the Black River at Black Rock in mid April.
episodes.157631: A stationary cold front draped to the south of the region and potent upper level disturbances approaching from Northern Mexico caused increasing wind shear and instability across portions of West Central Texas.  These features triggered isolated elevated severe thunderstorms near Abilene on April 14.  On April 15, more severe thunderstorms resulted in several large to very large hail storms.
episodes.157842: A wake low developed on the backside of a cluster of showers and thunderstorms racing south across southeast Louisiana. This drastically enhanced downdraft winds, producing long duration winds around tropical storm strength across the area with peak gusts as strong as a weak hurricane.
episodes.157875: A stalled frontal boundary combined with sufficient instability in place produced a thunderstorm over Lake Ponchartrain resulting in a couple severe wind reports.
episodes.157878: A stalled frontal boundary combined with sufficient instability in place produced a thunderstorm near Baton Rouge with severe hail.
episodes.158111: A cut off upper low slowly worked across the deep south during the middle of April. This produced multiple days of stormy weather.
episodes.158112: A cut off low slowly moved across the Deep South and produced multiple days of stormy weather. A few storms became severe during the period.
episodes.158147: Scattered severe thunderstorms in advance of a cold front produced damaging winds across portions of south central Virginia.
episodes.158193: A weak area of low pressure tracked east-northeast along a nearly stationary front over the northeast portion of central North Carolina during the evening. Widely scattered thunderstorms developed from Wake County north and east, where the best low level moisture existed at peak heating. A few storms along the front from South Hill, Virginia into the Kerr Lake, Lake Gaston, and Halifax areas exhibited weak rotation. In addition, large hail was reported in the storms over portions of the region with up to golf ball sized reported in Halifax County around sunset.
episodes.158301: Elevated convection developed during the late afternoon and evening well north of a cold front. A few storms produced marginally severe hail.
